Definition: Integration of farmer registries, agricultural input vouchers, land registrations, extension services data
Comments: No evidence of agriculture system integration into a data exchange platform.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score of 0 (Unknown) is revised to 1 (Not integrated). The same UNDP source already cited documents the absence of a national interoperability framework; the World Bank's Digital Eswatini Project Information Document (concept stage, 28 Jun 2025) confirms back-end interoperability and digital ID remain 'currently underdeveloped' and are only now being financed. Positive evidence that no exchange platform exists supports a score of 'Not integrated' rather than 'Unknown', consistent with the treatment already applied to the Planning & Statistics row in this dataset. revised_comments: Eswatini has no operational cross-government data exchange or interoperability framework, so agricultural data (farmer registries, input vouchers, land registration, extension services) is not integrated into any such platform. The World Bank-financed Digital Eswatini project, at concept stage in mid-2025, is only beginning to build the foundational interoperability and digital ID layers needed before sector-level integrations such as agriculture can be considered.

Definition: Integration of learner records, academic credentials, enrollment data, and scholarship/bursary systems
Comments: No evidence of education system integration into a data exchange platform. World Bank project plans digital connectivity for education institutions.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score of 0 (Unknown) is revised to 1 (Not integrated). The UNDP DRA confirms no national interoperability framework exists; the Ministry of ICT's Digital Government Implementation Roadmap Terms of Reference lists education services (student report access, transcript ordering, absenteeism alerting) only among roughly 200 services proposed for future digitisation, not yet delivered or integrated. World Bank's 2025 PID confirms interoperability is still underdeveloped. Positive evidence of non-integration supports score 1 rather than 0.
revised_comments: No education-sector data (learner records, credentials, enrolment, bursary systems) is integrated into a cross-government data exchange, because no such national interoperability platform yet exists in Eswatini. Government ICT planning documents list education services such as student report access and transcript ordering among services proposed for future digitisation under the Government in Your Hand programme, but these remain at the planning stage.

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government data exchange systems. 25 variables in 4 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Is artificial intelligence integrated into the data exchange for data quality, fraud detection or predictive analytics
Comments: No evidence of AI integrated into a data exchange system. UNDP Digital Readiness Assessment 2024 notes absence of an interoperability framework. AI capabilities not identified in data exchange context.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score of 0 (Unknown) is revised to 1 (No). Both the UNDP DRA (2024) and the World Bank Digital Eswatini PID (2025) confirm no national data exchange/interoperability platform exists into which AI could be embedded — this is positive evidence supporting 'No' rather than 'Unknown'. A related but distinct development was found and fetched: the Eswatini Revenue Service's May 2025 tender for a TaxCore-style fiscalisation system incorporating machine learning/AI for fraud detection. This is a single-agency system at RFP/early-deployment stage, not an AI capability functioning within a cross-government data exchange, so it does not support a higher score under this variable's definition.
revised_comments: No artificial intelligence capability is embedded within a national data exchange in Eswatini, because no such cross-government interoperability platform yet exists. Separately, the Eswatini Revenue Service is deploying a stand-alone fiscalisation system (TaxCore) that uses machine learning and AI for real-time tax fraud detection and predictive analytics, but this operates within a single agency rather than as part of an inter-agency data exchange.
